review.evidence: Compared the whole 2026-10-28 source with the guide. The rewritten macOS section keeps keyboard and pointing device as primary, gestures on Magic Trackpad, Magic Mouse and touch-surface controllers, touch as secondary on a touch-display Mac or an iPad through Sidecar, and all six new rules. Standard gestures now show touch (or pinch) and hold on all six platforms and double tap opening an item on a touch-display Mac, with Series 9 and later and Ultra 2 and later for the Watch primary action. The new macOS trackpad and touch display table matches all seven rows. Unchanged content is still kept: best practices, custom gestures, iOS/iPadOS gestures, tvOS, visionOS indirect/direct gestures, custom gestures and system overlays, and watchOS double tap. The change log adds October 28, 2026. I found no omission or wrong statement.

Checked: keyboard and pointing device primary, standard gestures on Magic Trackpad, Magic Mouse and touch-surface game controllers, and direct touch as a secondary mode on a touch-display Mac or an iPad through Sidecar are the opening of the guide's #macOS.
Checked: keep the layout and size of elements unchanged when supporting touch, because touch is secondary and people switch inputs often, is the first #macOS bullet.
Checked: enlarge tap targets, not controls, so touches slightly outside the visible bounds still hit, and standard controls get a suitable tap target automatically, is the second #macOS bullet.

Checked: expandable controls for small or dense controls (temporary touch-sized variant on tap, usable while held, stays briefly after lift; automatic for standard steppers, sliders and dials) are the third #macOS bullet.

Checked: touch must never be the only route (every function needs keyboard and pointer), and touch equivalents for pointer-only actions such as Shift-drag or hover menus, with the link to Pointing devices #macOS as in the source, are the fourth #macOS bullet.
Checked: preserving gestures people know from the app on iPhone or iPad or from a trackpad or Magic Mouse, and testing for conflicts with macOS system gestures, is the fifth #macOS bullet.
Checked: custom gestures must work for both direct touch and the trackpad, with modifier keys where needed, is the sixth #macOS bullet.
